messages.content: Contemplate on few lines of “Part four” (page 153) of this novel, “Majid: Wake up, Bibi. I am going to take both of you to the village. When Majeed came out of the house carrying Jamila, wrapped in a thin... quilt, a bewilderedRahima at his heels, the brilliant moonlight at first blinded him.” Even if Majeed was mostly depicted as a cunning and apathetic person throughout the narrative, do you find the same character traits in the mentioned lines? Was he trying to save Rahima and Jamila out of good-will (deontology) or his action was well-calculated (teleology)?Explain it. Include at least 10 single-word palindromes, each at least 5 characters long.

message.content: The moonlight blinds Majeed, yet his intent remains opaque. Is this a moment of sudden **civic** duty or a calculated move? The scene feels like a **level** shift in his cold demeanor. He acts with a **radar**-like precision, not warmth. This is not pure **goodwill**; it is a **kayak** through moral waters. His choice is a **refer** to self-preservation. It lacks the **stressed** emotion of true care. Instead, it is a **deified** act of control. The outcome matters more than the motive. This is **teleology**, not deontology. He saves them because it serves his purpose. The action is a **solos** performance of power. There is no **stats** data on his heart. Only the result counts for him.
